clue.text: Certainly tears when audit reports are due?

parts.note: yea is an old word of assent, yes or certainly
tears as a verb, rips apart, means rends

explanation.surface: Sobbing accountants weep as the deadline for audit reports approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping, but it is the verb for ripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are closed and audited at the close of the financial year, so these are the times reports fall due.

clue.text: One avoiding harm, staying ahead of a lot of mean snakes

indicators.note: staying ahead of puts the first piece in front of the next
avoiding says the word for one is left out of the word for harm

parts.note: to harm badly is to maim
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: mean, as in low or contemptible, is base

explanation.surface: Someone keeping out of danger stays ahead of a group of nasty snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIM without I gives MAM; BASE cut short by 'a lot of' gives BAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mambas are venomous African snakes, so the plural answer names some snakes.

clue.text: Most of holiday locked in prison? That leads to split

indicators.note: locked in says the shortened holiday goes inside the word for prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison

indicators.note: Most of says the last letter of the word for holiday is dropped

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday

explanation.surface: Spending most of your holiday in jail might well lead to a break-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a division or split, as between groups or along a crystal's plane.

clue.text: Independent avoiding stories on native teaching

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second
avoiding says the letter for Independent is left out of the word for stories

parts.note: stories, as in fibs, are lies
a son of a place is a native of it

explanation.surface: An independent school avoids made-up tales when teaching about a native people.
explanation.walkthrough: LIES without I gives LES, placed above SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a unit of teaching, an instructive session given to pupils.

clue.text: Chewing item involving a lot of saliva and tooth

indicators.note: involving says the chewing item wraps round the shortened saliva

parts.note: cud is the food a cow chews again

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word for saliva, losing its last letter

parts.note: spit is saliva

explanation.surface: Something chewed, dripping with saliva, involves a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuspid is a canine, a pointed tooth with a single cusp.

clue.text: Beginning to accept America after Democrat's Hollywoodised vision?

indicators.note: to accept says the word for beginning takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a beginning is a start

indicators.note: after says the America piece follows the Democrat letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A political pundit sneers at a Democrat's glossy, movie-made picture of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' looks like an instruction to take a first letter, but it is a synonym in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is the dreamy glamour of showbusiness, a romantic vision of the kind Hollywood sells.

clue.text: Boundless amorous activity — it's a capital sort of thing!

indicators.note: Boundless says the outer letters of the word for amorous activity are removed

parts.note: snogging is British slang for kissing and cuddling

explanation.surface: A cheerful boast that endless canoodling is a first-class pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like 'excellent', but it means of the head: SNOGGING loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is informal for the head, and capital comes from Latin for head.

clue.text: Deplore security with our team getting back inside

indicators.note: inside says the turned word goes within the security word

parts.note: bail is money given as security for an accused person

indicators.note: getting back says the word for our team is turned round

parts.note: our team, the people speaking, are we

explanation.surface: A fan laments the security arrangements as the home side returns to the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewail something is to lament it loudly, expressing strong regret, much as deploring does.

clue.text: Expression of relationship quite in error about a cricket side

indicators.note: about says the jumbled quite goes round the letter a
in error says the letters of quite are mistakenly arranged

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A batsman's quite wrong about which side of the field is which.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, also called the leg side, is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics an equation states the equality of two quantities, expressing how they relate.

clue.text: Collections of gifts — jokes about priest dropping one

indicators.note: about says the jokes go round the shortened priest

parts.note: gags are jokes

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for one falls away from the word for priest

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader, loosely a priest
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Bundles of presents are filled with jokes about a priest losing something.
explanation.definitionFit: A grab bag is a lucky dip of wrapped presents, a mixed collection to pick from.

clue.text: Polish dumplings I brought in for American soldier

indicators.note: brought in says the letter I is set within the word for for

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
GI is the usual name for an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier abroad has Polish dumplings brought to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' disguises itself with its capital as the start of the sentence, but it is the nation, not shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierogi or pirogi are filled boiled dumplings, a staple of Polish cooking.

clue.text: Marked by liquid inside tank, sloshing around

indicators.note: sloshing around describes liquid churning, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Something got splashed as liquid sloshed around in a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink is a liquid, and something blotted with spilt ink has been marked by it.

clue.text: Say "Good cheer"

parts.note: say, meaning for example, is e.g.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Good cheer' looks like one phrase but splits: Good gives G and cheer is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or encourage them, as cheering spectators do.

clue.text: What setter may have to deal with — a selection of unhelpful names

definitions.text: What setter may have to deal

indicators.note: selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crossword setter grumbles about having to handle a batch of awkward names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler, but it is a bone-setter, who fixes fractures.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone-setter treats broken bones, and this forearm bone is one he may have to deal with.

clue.text: School bound to exclude a stupid person

indicators.note: to exclude says the letter a is dropped from the word for bound

parts.note: a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A school is obliged to expel a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' reads as obliged, but it is a jump: LEAP loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Schlep is Yiddish-derived slang for a clumsy, foolish or ineffectual oaf.

clue.text: I left, after entering country American abandoned eagerly

indicators.note: entering says I and the letter for left go inside the shortened country
abandoned says the letter for American is left out of the country

parts.note: Hungary is a country of central Europe

explanation.surface: A traveller's account of leaving a country that an American had deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: HUNGARY without A gives HUNGRY, with IL entering it.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something with keen appetite or desire is to do it eagerly, as if starving for it.

clue.text: Select in audio or visual?

indicators.note: in audio says the word is heard, not written, giving a word spoken the same way

parts.note: to select is to pick

explanation.surface: Choose between a sound recording and a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets audio against visual, while 'in audio' is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pic is an informal picture or photo, something visual as opposed to heard.

clue.text: Scottish town sees soldier with work unit returning

indicators.note: returning says the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so soldier gives ant
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A Scottish town sees a soldier come back with a working party.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTERG read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gretna, just over the border, is the Scottish town famed for runaway weddings at Gretna Green.

clue.text: Gun salesman having US gun with cap off

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative

indicators.note: with cap off says the first letter of the word for US gun is removed

parts.note: heater is American slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: A salesman carries an American firearm with its cap removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is a firearm that fires several shots without reloading.

clue.text: Exeter flailing around line under a crossbar

indicators.note: in a down clue, under says this part goes below the letter a
around says the mixed city letters go round the letter for line
flailing says the letters of the city are thrashed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Exeter, the city in Devon, flails about a line drawn under some crossbar.
explanation.walkthrough: EXETER rearranged to XETREE goes around L, giving XLETREE beneath A.
explanation.definitionFit: An axletree is the fixed bar running across beneath a cart, on which the wheels turn.

clue.text: Wife being embraced by lover will make you cringe

indicators.note: being embraced by says the wife letter goes inside the word for lover

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something

explanation.surface: Watching a wife being hugged by her lover is enough to make anyone wince.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to grovel or behave servilely, the sense of cringe as abject flattery.

clue.text: Nerdy expert right about an English symbol? On the contrary

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other
On the contrary flips the clue's stated order, so the symbol goes round the letter for right

parts.note: the oak tree is a traditional emblem of England

explanation.surface: A geek is right about something being an English emblem, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, right goes about the symbol; 'On the contrary' swaps that, so OAK goes round R after AN.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive enthusiast, a nerd who knows all the details.

clue.text: A policeman returning to apprehend church board — that's OK?

indicators.note: to apprehend means to arrest, so the turned policeman holds the church letters inside
returning says the policeman's letters are read backwards

parts.note: PC is a police constable
CE is the Church of England
a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A constable heads back to arrest the church committee, and wonders if that's allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: PC reversed is CP, which holds CE to give CCEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable is satisfactory or tolerable, which is just what OK means.

clue.text: Three letters enthralling me, outlining description of bomb?

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the three-letter span holds the note inside

parts.note: the three letters a, b, c run from A to C
me, the third note in tonic sol-fa, is also written mi

explanation.surface: A letter writer captivated, sketching how a bomb might be described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three letters' is A TO C, which captures MI; 'outlining' just joins this to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom bomb is the classic nuclear weapon, so the adjective names that kind of bomb.

clue.text: See about following cook after cutting dairy product …

indicators.note: following says the jumbled see comes after the trimmed cook
after cutting says the cook word is trimmed, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chef is a cook

indicators.note: about says the letters of see are moved round

explanation.surface: A chef, having trimmed something, turns to the dairy product.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEF loses its F to give CHE; SEE rearranged gives ESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is made from milk curds, a standard product of the dairy.

clue.text: … for each dish eaten by expert

indicators.note: eaten by says the dish goes inside the word for expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: An expert eats one dish for every person.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, as in a pound apiece.

clue.text: Judge Independent's backed working newspaperman

parts.note: the Independent speaking of itself as its own, so the newspaper's is ours, giving our

indicators.note: backed says the word for working is turned back

parts.note: a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A judge sitting on behalf of the Independent backs a working reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper refers to itself: what is the Independent's is OUR. ON reversed gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Journo is informal slang for a journalist, someone who writes for a newspaper.

clue.text: Thin letter from Greece — one arrived after going round about

indicators.note: going round about says the whole string is turned to face the other way

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
one is the Roman numeral I
came means arrived

explanation.surface: A letter from Greece comes after a long roundabout journey.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA, I and CAME make ETAICAME, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make abnormally thin, wasting the body away.

clue.text: After move to new stop, I sold various newspapers

indicators.note: After says the jumbled letters come after the key

parts.note: the tab key moves a typewriter carriage or cursor to the next tab stop

indicators.note: various says the letters of I sold appear in a varied order

explanation.surface: After moving to a new bus stop, a vendor sold assorted newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' suggests a bus, but it is a tab stop on a typewriter or keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabloids are compact-format popular papers, a type of newspaper.

clue.text: Area of Greater Manchester suitable for religious folk in brief

indicators.note: in brief says the long word is cut short to its abbreviated form

parts.note: ecclesiastical means relating to the church and its clergy

explanation.surface: A district near Manchester, briefly described as fit for the devout.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, famous for Eccles cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles is a town within the Salford borough of Greater Manchester in north-west England.
